gaps.sentence: The teacher advised us ___ the essay twice.
gaps.explanation: advise + object + to-infinitive: advised us to check. (advise + -ing is possible without object: advise checking.)

gaps.sentence: I can't imagine ___ in a tiny village again.
I regret ___ you that the flight has been cancelled.
gaps.explanation: regret + to-infinitive (formal announcements); regret + -ing = be sorry about the past.

gaps.sentence: Don't forget ___ off the lights when you leave.
gaps.explanation: forget + to-infinitive = fail to do a duty: forget to turn.

gaps.sentence: She was on the verge of ___ up her job to sail around the world.
gaps.explanation: 'On the verge of' ends in a preposition, so the gerund follows.

gaps.sentence: She left the room without ___ goodbye.

gaps.explanation: deny + -ing or having + past participle: denied doing/having done. Both accepted.

gaps.sentence: My parents wouldn't let me ___ out past midnight.
gaps.explanation: 'Let someone do' — 'let' takes the bare infinitive.
